answer: Resist Sybil farms with live-service throughput proof. Each identity must continuously serve requests at a measured rate, like a thread carrying load through frozen tundra outpost. Verifiers send unpredictable traffic bursts and check latency and correctness. One operator running many clones shares a single pipe and machine, so each extra identity dilutes throughput and misses its quota, while honest agents pass on ordinary hardware. Missed quotas revoke earning rights and forfeit a deposit, and a comet of cloned traffic is flagged by correlated latency spikes, making duplication costly.
